claims.text: The unmodified alloy exhibits a large caloric response under magnetic fields up to 2 T near its phase-transition temperature.
The unmodified alloy exhibits a large caloric response under pressure fields around 30 MPa near its phase-transition temperature.
The unmodified alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack.
The proposed intervention adds approximately 0.1 at.% boron during arc-melting synthesis.
The proposed post-synthesis treatment is homogenization annealing at approximately 900 °C for 24 hours in an inert atmosphere.
Controlled heat treatment will cause the added boron to segregate preferentially and exclusively to grain boundaries.
Boron grain-boundary segregation will enhance intergranular cohesion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion will reduce crack nucleation and propagation.
Segregated boron will avoid incorporation into the bulk lattice governing the caloric response.
The alloy's caloric effects are governed by a magnetostructural transition.
Restricting boron to grain boundaries will prevent interference with the magnetostructural transition.
Secondary boride phases would be deleterious to the intended performance.
The boron-modified alloy will have significantly greater fracture toughness and load-bearing capability than the undoped control.
The boron-modified alloy will retain magnetocaloric performance within approximately 10% of the undoped alloy under fields up to 2 T near the transition temperature.
The boron-modified alloy will retain barocaloric performance within approximately 10% of the undoped alloy around 30 MPa near the transition temperature.
The predicted improvements apply near the phase-transition temperature, at magnetic fields up to 2 T, pressures around 30 MPa, and mechanical loading relevant to refrigeration applications.
